main.title: Wii Sports Resort
main.subtitle: Twelve sports share one island
main.summary: Wii Sports Resort is Nintendo's Wii sports collection set around Wuhu Island, expanding the approach of Wii Sports with twelve activities and the Wii MotionPlus accessory. A first arrival by parachute introduces the holiday setting before players move between contests on the water, in the air and on land. Mii characters keep the participants familiar, while the island gives the separate sports a shared home. Its bays, cliffs and buildings become landmarks that can be encountered from several different viewpoints as the collection moves between activities.

cards.heading: Twelve sports share one island
cards.text: Wii Sports Resort is Nintendo's Wii sports collection set around Wuhu Island, expanding the approach of Wii Sports with twelve activities and the Wii MotionPlus accessory. A first arrival by parachute introduces the holiday setting before players move between contests on the water, in the air and on land. Mii characters keep the participants familiar, while the island gives the separate sports a shared home. Its bays, cliffs and buildings become landmarks that can be encountered from several different viewpoints as the collection moves between activities.

cards.heading: A small rotation changes the result
cards.text: MotionPlus gives the Remote more detailed orientation tracking, allowing sports to respond to the angle as well as the broad direction of a movement. In table tennis, twisting during the swing changes the spin applied to the ball. Archery uses the Remote and Nunchuk together as bow and string, translating a recognisable physical pose into aiming and releasing an arrow. The activities introduce their own versions of the same promise: moving the controller deliberately should produce a difference that can be seen and understood in the resulting action.

cards.heading: A holiday can become a competition
cards.text: Bowling and golf return beside new sports including swordplay and basketball, giving the collection both recognisable starting points and unfamiliar activities to learn. Several events support players taking turns with a shared controller, while others allow direct competition. Free flight over Wuhu Island offers another reason to notice the setting between contests. The collection makes the accessory's improved precision useful through these different forms of play, allowing a casual first attempt to develop into a repeated challenge once friends understand how a particular movement affects the result.

main.title: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies
main.subtitle: A guardian among mortals
main.summary: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies is Level-5 and Square Enix's Nintendo DS role-playing adventure about a Celestrian stranded in the mortal world. The player creates this fallen guardian and the companions who travel alongside them. Towns, monsters and quests retain the series' approachable fantasy style, but local multiplayer lets friends enter the journey together. The personalised party gives the adventure a different emphasis from following a fixed cast. Its heroes can look like the player's own group, preparing for the same discoveries and battles.

cards.heading: A guardian among mortals
cards.text: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies is Level-5 and Square Enix's Nintendo DS role-playing adventure about a Celestrian stranded in the mortal world. The player creates this fallen guardian and the companions who travel alongside them. Towns, monsters and quests retain the series' approachable fantasy style, but local multiplayer lets friends enter the journey together. The personalised party gives the adventure a different emphasis from following a fixed cast. Its heroes can look like the player's own group, preparing for the same discoveries and battles.

cards.heading: Build the party before the encounter
cards.text: Monsters are visible while exploring, so an encounter begins when the party makes contact rather than arriving only as an unseen interruption. Battles use familiar turn-based commands for attacks, abilities, spells, items and defence. The player can direct each companion or assign automated tactics. Creating the other party members makes their preparation part of the same process as designing the protagonist. A balanced group needs more than a distinctive appearance: equipment, available abilities and the role of each traveller determine what happens when a visible threat finally catches them.

cards.heading: A journey that travels with its owner
cards.text: Optional quests and an alchemy system provide reasons to gather ingredients, inspect treasure and keep playing beyond the next story destination. The handheld format also supports local communication, including the exchange of treasure maps through its anonymous communication mode. That feature made carrying the game through a crowded place part of its appeal in Japan. Dragon Quest IX connects the long, private routines of a role-playing adventure with the possibility of encountering somebody else's progress, allowing a portable machine to carry both a party and an invitation.

main.title: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies
main.summary: Level-5 and Square Enix bring the main Dragon Quest series to DS, with a customisable hero, turn-based battles and local cooperative adventuring.

cards.heading: A Celestrian's fall begins a portable Dragon Quest
cards.text: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies reached Nintendo DS in Japan in July 2009, followed by an international release in 2010. Developed by Level-5 and Square Enix, it follows a Celestrian searching the mortal world for magical fruits scattered by a disaster. Players create a hero and take part in turn-based battles, with local multiplayer allowing friends to share the adventure.

cards.heading: Level-5 and Yuji Horii choose the Nintendo DS
cards.text: Concept work for a new mainline Dragon Quest game began after development wrapped up on Dragon Quest VIII, with Horii and the rest of the series staff deciding what platform the next mainline entry should be developed for, with Horii wanting to reach as wide an audience as possible. Hino later noted that he suggested the DS as the platform from an early stage, inspired by its widespread commercial success; Level-5 was already working with the DS developing Professor Layton and the Curious Village. After some hesitation about having a mainline entry on a portable platform, Horii was convinced. Production began in 2005, with Horii keeping its production as secret as possible. During production it went by the codename "Xenlon", named by Ichimura during a conversation in a store called Xenlon Tokyo.

cards.heading: A multiplayer experiment returns to turn-based battles
cards.text: During early stages and with its original trailer, Dragon Quest IX broke with series tradition and used an action-based combat system to fit into the multiplayer design. This design approach was first proposed by Hino. Horii explained that this was a prototype design, and after first showing it off it drew heated criticism from series fans and prompted arguments online. Paired with Horii finding that turn-based gameplay still worked and was enjoyable in multiplayer, and that prolonged action combat became "monotonous", the battle system was switched back to the standard turn-based design. The sprite-based monster encounters were taken from the spin-off Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker so players had more control over when they got into battle. The quest system was designed with short play sessions in mind. Ichimura elaborated that the quest system drew inspiration from The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, while Diablo was used as a reference on keeping players engaged for long periods.

cards.heading: Four adventurers share quests and treasure maps
cards.text: Up to four players can connect locally, with one hosting the adventure. Guests can travel with the host or explore separately, keeping the items, experience and gold they earn, though the host's story progress remains separate. Tag Mode uses the sleeping DS to exchange characters and treasure maps with nearby systems. Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection supplied additional online functions until the service closed in 2014.

cards.heading: Koichi Sugiyama writes for an angelic atmosphere
cards.text: Horii supplied Koichi Sugiyama with scenes and the atmosphere each needed, including an angelic quality suited to the story. The score was then prepared for the DS sound environment, drawing on Sugiyama's experience with the Dragon Quest V remake. Music changed through testing: an early battle theme bored Horii during play, and the opening of the familiar Overture was repeatedly revised. For a key early scene, Sugiyama also timed instrumental details to the image, letting a harp enter as light appeared from above.

main.title: 'Splosion Man
main.subtitle: Explode to leave the laboratory
main.summary: 'Splosion Man is Twisted Pixel's Xbox Live Arcade platform game, released on 22 July 2009. A living experiment escapes through the Big Science laboratory by repeatedly detonating himself. The explosion is his jump, weapon and means of breaking obstacles, giving the player one central action with several uses. A room becomes a question about where and when that action should happen. The comic presentation makes the escape deliberately ridiculous, but the movement asks for careful timing as the player chains blasts through machinery and hazards that leave little space for a mistake.

cards.heading: Explode to leave the laboratory
cards.text: 'Splosion Man is Twisted Pixel's Xbox Live Arcade platform game, released on 22 July 2009. A living experiment escapes through the Big Science laboratory by repeatedly detonating himself. The explosion is his jump, weapon and means of breaking obstacles, giving the player one central action with several uses. A room becomes a question about where and when that action should happen. The comic presentation makes the escape deliberately ridiculous, but the movement asks for careful timing as the player chains blasts through machinery and hazards that leave little space for a mistake.

cards.heading: Three blasts have to reach the next safe place
cards.text: Only three consecutive explosions are available before a cooldown, so a route must include a way to recover before continuing. The player uses walls, platforms and other objects to turn those limited actions into height or distance. An enemy can also become part of the route if exploding at the right moment removes it and carries the character onward. Repeated attempts reveal how a room is arranged. What first looks like a series of unrelated hazards gradually becomes one sequence whose movements need to connect without wasting the available blasts.

cards.heading: One action carries a cooperative challenge
cards.text: Separate multiplayer levels ask players to coordinate their explosions, turning timing into a shared problem rather than simply placing several people in the solo campaign. The game arrived during the 2009 Summer of Arcade promotion and was well received for the clarity of its idea and challenge. Xbox Live players selected it as their best original XBLA game that year. Ms. Splosion Man followed in 2011. The original demonstrates how much variation can come from a tightly limited verb when the surrounding rooms keep finding different reasons for the player to use it.

main.title: Katamari Forever
main.subtitle: Roll the colour back into memory
main.summary: Katamari Forever is Genki's PlayStation 3 entry in the rolling action-puzzle series, released in Japan on 23 July 2009. The King of All Cosmos has lost his memory, while the Prince and his cousins have created a troublesome robotic substitute. Part of the adventure takes place inside the King's mind, where gathering objects restores colour to black-and-white scenes. Other assignments ask for new stars after RoboKing's mistakes. The familiar act of growing an adhesive ball now connects two problems: recovering a person's memories and repairing the sky.

cards.heading: Roll the colour back into memory
cards.text: Katamari Forever is Genki's PlayStation 3 entry in the rolling action-puzzle series, released in Japan on 23 July 2009. The King of All Cosmos has lost his memory, while the Prince and his cousins have created a troublesome robotic substitute. Part of the adventure takes place inside the King's mind, where gathering objects restores colour to black-and-white scenes. Other assignments ask for new stars after RoboKing's mistakes. The familiar act of growing an adhesive ball now connects two problems: recovering a person's memories and repairing the sky.

cards.heading: A collection of places to revisit
cards.text: Most of the game's thirty-four stages draw on earlier Katamari adventures, with a small number of new settings. Returning routes acquire a different role through their presentation and objectives, inviting players to recognise the surroundings while finding another way through them. Size still decides which objects can be collected. A space that first requires careful movement between chairs and shelves can later become something the whole ball overwhelms. The changing scale remains the source of both the route's practical choices and its escalating visual joke.

cards.heading: A small hop changes the route
cards.text: The Prince Hop lets the katamari leave the ground, adding a way to clear a small obstacle or reach an awkward object. King Shock briefly pulls nearby items toward the ball, giving another means of gathering a dense cluster. Different visual treatments and rearranged music reinforce the game's role as a return through the series. Local multiplayer adds a shared or competitive version of the rolling. Its Japanese title, Katamari Damacy Tribute, expresses that retrospective character particularly clearly: it revisits familiar spaces while giving them a new frame.

main.title: Monster Hunter Tri
main.subtitle: Hunting beneath the surface
main.summary: On August 1, 2009 Monster Hunter Tri arrived on Wii in Japan.

cards.heading: The hunt moves underwater
cards.text: Monster Hunter Tri arrived on Wii in Japan on August 1, 2009. Capcom introduced underwater hunting, adding another direction from which creatures could approach. Solo quests, four-player online hunts and local arena play continued the series' emphasis on preparation, equipment and learning a monster's behaviour.

cards.heading: Developing underwater hunting
cards.text: The ecosystems in Monster Hunter Tri have been expanded to include underwater environments. Director Kaname Fujioka, in a 2017 interview, said that they wanted to include underwater sections and combat in Monster Hunter, both to try something different from what other games have done with this, and trying to see how underwater combat would work. While it was included in Tri, Fujioka said that the amount of effort they needed to program these sections took too much time away from what other parts they could develop, and generally have left underwater combat out of future Monster Hunter games, but would like to come back to it sometime in the future.

cards.heading: Four-player online quests
cards.text: Monster Hunter Tri on the Wii offered an online component where up to 4 players can venture on new quests together, represented by the character traveling to a nearby city harbor port. The game uses the same character data as the single-player offering, letting players continue to build up better equipment from quest rewards within either mode. Quests in this mode featured more difficult monsters than the single player game due to the added players available to fight. Quests are broken out into a number of ranks, requiring players to complete all quests in a rank before moving to a new tier. A limited selection of the items that the player can collect can be traded with other players here or while on a quest, typically limited to healing and restorative items, preventing the trading of equipment, monster parts, or resources necessary to make better equipment. The Wii version's online service has since been shut down.

cards.heading: Forging equipment from monster materials
cards.text: To progress in the game, the player is typically required to collect parts of the larger monsters that they are assigned to kill, and using those to forge or upgrade weapons and armor. By being able to take on higher-ranked Guild quests with improved equipment, the player will gain access to a larger array of monster parts and world resources that lead to better equipment they can then craft.

main.title: MagnaCarta 2
main.subtitle: An amnesiac joins a larger struggle
main.summary: MagnaCarta 2 is Softmax's Xbox 360 role-playing game, first released in South Korea on 6 August 2009. Juto becomes involved with Zephie and the conflict around her, entering a story whose larger history he does not initially understand. The game continues the Magna Carta name with a new adventure built for seventh-generation console hardware. Exploration moves directly into battles on the field, keeping the party within the same surroundings. Its combat combines active movement with systems that make the timing of a character change important to the progress of an encounter.

cards.heading: An amnesiac joins a larger struggle
cards.text: MagnaCarta 2 is Softmax's Xbox 360 role-playing game, first released in South Korea on 6 August 2009. Juto becomes involved with Zephie and the conflict around her, entering a story whose larger history he does not initially understand. The game continues the Magna Carta name with a new adventure built for seventh-generation console hardware. Exploration moves directly into battles on the field, keeping the party within the same surroundings. Its combat combines active movement with systems that make the timing of a character change important to the progress of an encounter.

cards.heading: Change the active fighter before the rhythm breaks
cards.text: The player moves between an exploration stance and a slower combat stance, choosing when to engage the enemies nearby. Three characters can be active, with others available to replace them. Normal attacks and abilities interact with Kan, the energy used by special actions, giving the party another resource to manage alongside health. The player has to consider how one character's activity affects the next. A useful sequence involves more than staying with the strongest fighter, since changing control can help the group sustain its actions through a longer confrontation.

cards.heading: A Korean role-playing studio on Xbox 360
cards.text: The game uses Unreal Engine 3, with character art and presentation forming a prominent part of Softmax's approach to the console generation. Sung-woon Jang directed its sound and composed the music. Namco Bandai published the release, which reached Japan shortly after South Korea and North America and Europe in October 2009. It remained exclusive to Xbox 360. MagnaCarta 2 offers another perspective on that console's role-playing catalogue, bringing a Korean-developed series into the same international market where Microsoft was also promoting projects from established Japanese studios.

main.title: Trials HD
main.subtitle: One motorcycle, one difficult line
main.summary: Trials HD is RedLynx's Xbox Live Arcade motorcycle game, released on 12 August 2009. A rider crosses obstacle courses shown from the side, using throttle, braking and body position to keep the bike moving towards the finish. The route is easy to understand and often difficult to complete. A wheel placed slightly too far forward can turn a promising attempt into another crash. Three-dimensional scenery gives the course depth, but the action stays on one plane, keeping the next obstacle and the rider's balance clearly connected.

cards.heading: One motorcycle, one difficult line
cards.text: Trials HD is RedLynx's Xbox Live Arcade motorcycle game, released on 12 August 2009. A rider crosses obstacle courses shown from the side, using throttle, braking and body position to keep the bike moving towards the finish. The route is easy to understand and often difficult to complete. A wheel placed slightly too far forward can turn a promising attempt into another crash. Three-dimensional scenery gives the course depth, but the action stays on one plane, keeping the next obstacle and the rider's balance clearly connected.

cards.heading: Learn what the wheels are doing
cards.text: Leaning changes the bike's pitch on the ground and in the air. A steep face may require the front wheel to rise first, while a landing asks the rider to arrive at the right angle. Restarting gives an immediate chance to try a different movement. Times and faults measure progress separately, so reaching the finish can be followed by an attempt to do it cleanly. Courses range from introductory tracks to extreme challenges, gradually demanding more precise control of the same small set of actions.

cards.heading: Build the obstacle that stops a friend
cards.text: A level editor lets players construct courses from the tools used for the game's own tracks and share them with friends. Leaderboards and replays provide another way to study a difficult section, including the controller inputs behind a successful run. Skill games take the motorcycle into unusual challenges, such as towing a dangerous load or performing flips. Trials HD arrived during Microsoft's Summer of Arcade promotion and helped establish the series on consoles. Its repeated attempts work because each failure makes a small physical problem easier to recognise.

main.title: Batman: Arkham Asylum
main.summary: Batman: Arkham Asylum is a 2009 action-adventure game developed by Rocksteady Studios and published by Eidos Interactive in conjunction with Warner Bros.

cards.heading: The Joker takes over Arkham
cards.text: Batman: Arkham Asylum is a 2009 action-adventure game developed by Rocksteady Studios and published by Eidos Interactive in conjunction with Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment. Based on the DC Comics superhero Batman and written by veteran Batman writer Paul Dini, Arkham Asylum was inspired by the long-running comic book mythos. In the game's main storyline, Batman battles his archenemy, the  Joker, who instigates an elaborate plot to seize control of Arkham Asylum, trap Batman inside with many of his incarcerated foes, and threaten Gotham City with hidden bombs.

cards.heading: Combat, stealth and investigation
cards.text: The game is presented from the third-person perspective with a primary focus on Batman's combat and stealth abilities, detective skills, and gadgets that can be used in combat and exploration. Batman can freely move around the Arkham Asylum facility, interacting with characters and undertaking missions, and unlocking new areas by progressing through the main story or obtaining new equipment. The player is able to deviate away from the main story to unlock additional content and collectible items. Combat focuses on chaining attacks together against numerous foes while avoiding damage, while stealth allows Batman to conceal himself around an area, using gadgets and the environment to silently eliminate enemies.

cards.heading: Developing the asylum
cards.text: Development began at Rocksteady Studios in May 2007, with a 40-person team that expanded to 60 people by the project's conclusion after approximately 21 months. Among other sources, the game design was inspired by the Batman comics of Neal Adams and Frank Miller, as well as Grant Morrison and Dave McKean's graphic novel Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth. Built on Unreal Engine 3, Arkham Asylum's production underwent several variations, refining both gameplay such as the combat system, and the central story, resulting in the removal of plot elements and some of Batman's main enemies, who did not fit the tone of the rest of the game. Rocksteady began developing ideas for a sequel months before Arkham Asylum's completion, hiding hints to the sequel within the game.

cards.heading: Reception and later editions
cards.text: Arkham Asylum was released worldwide for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 video game consoles in August 2009, followed by a Windows version. The game received critical acclaim, particularly for its narrative, atmosphere and combat, though some criticism was directed at its boss fights. Upon release, many reviewers called it the "greatest comic book game of all time." It won several awards, including Best Action Adventure game, Best Game, and Game of the Year from various media outlets, and it held the Guinness World Record for "Most Critically Acclaimed Superhero Game Ever". It has been cited as one of the greatest video games ever made. The game received a "Game of the Year Edition" in 2010, and a remastered version for the PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in 2016. A version for the Nintendo Switch was released in 2023.

cards.heading: The beginning of the Arkham series
cards.text: Arkham Asylum's success launched the Batman: Arkham series, comprising video game sequels and spin-offs, comic books, merchandise, and an animated film, beginning in 2011 with the game's narrative sequel Arkham City.

main.title: Guitar Hero 5
main.subtitle: The band line-up becomes a choice rather than a rule
main.summary: Guitar Hero 5 emphasised flexible instrument combinations and uninterrupted Party Play, with every disc song available from the start.

cards.heading: A band on your own terms
cards.text: Released first in North America on September 1, 2009, Guitar Hero 5 kept the full-band format while loosening its rules. Up to four players can choose any combination of guitar, bass, drums and vocals, including several copies of the same instrument. The disc contains 85 songs by 83 artists, all available immediately in Quickplay. Neversoft’s design makes the group’s preferred roles more important than filling a prescribed band line-up.

cards.heading: Let the next player join in
cards.text: Party Play lets people enter or leave without stopping the current song. Career mode adds instrument-specific challenges, giving familiar tracks new objectives. A music studio and compatibility with earlier downloadable songs extend the available repertoire beyond the disc.
